_about: Philip Schaff (1819-1893), The Creeds of Christendom, with a History and Critical Notes (New York: Harper, 1877-1878, 3 vols): I, The History of Creeds; II, The Greek and Latin Creeds, with Translations; III, The Evangelical Protestant Creeds, with Translations, the Lutheran and Reformed confessions and catechisms in their original languages with English translations. All three are Internet Archive OCR of Harper's 1878 printing (title pages read: 'Volume I. The History of Creeds', 'Volume II. The Greek and Latin Creeds', 'Volume III. Evangelical Protestant Creeds, with Translations', New York: Harper, 1878). Vols. II and III are mostly Greek, Latin and German in parallel columns, so their English word share is low by nature. Princeton's vol. III has a short pamphlet by James I. Good on the Synod of Dort bound in ahead of the title page. CCEL's proofed texts are pending (see _pending): its vols. I-II are the 1931 sixth edition, and its vol. III is keyed from a 1977 reprint. 2026-11-03 (Adam's Libronix inventory): History of the Christian Church, all eight volumes, from CCEL (vols. V-VI, the Middle Ages, are by his son David S. Schaff, published 1907 and 1910). The 1931 sixth edition of the Creeds, vols. I-II (CCEL), added 2026-11-03 by the non-renewal sweep: never renewed.

_pending.ccel creeds3 (The Creeds of Christendom,: Moved here 2026-10-03 after review cycle 11. CCEL's proofed vol. III is keyed from Baker Book House's 1977 photographic reprint ('reprinted by arrangement with' Harper; CCEL's print-source field says '1889 (Baker reprint)'), whose text carries copyrights of 1877, 1905 and 1919 and nothing later, so the words are almost certainly public domain in the US; but the edition CCEL keyed is a post-1930 printing, and it lacks Part First (the Lutheran creeds). Adam's call whether to prefer CCEL's proofed text over the 1878 OCR now held as schaff-creeds-3-1878.

_nonrenewal.schaff-creeds-1-1931: Non-renewal sweep 2026-11-03 (Adam: "I want everything that was not renewed"). CCEL keyed it from the sixth edition (Harper, New York, 1931; preface dated January 1931), revised by David S. Schaff, American, so a US work (URAA does not reach it). pipeline/renewal_check.py over NYPL's cce-renewals (every renewal 1950-1991), by surname plus title words and by title alone: no renewal of The Creeds of Christendom (due 1958-59; the only title hit is Gerrish's 1963 Faith of Christendom). US public domain by non-renewal; the 1878 text it revises was public domain already.
